findings.title: Replace refs and info/grafts make a DIVERGED repository read LOCAL-BEHIND: plain run exits 0 (false clean)
findings.detail: classify() decides ancestry with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, which honours refs/replace/* and .git/info/grafts of the repository under examination. Reproduced in scratch: owned repo with local c3 and remote c2 both children of c1, objects fetched: verifier exit 12 DIVERGED. After `git replace <c2> <fake commit with parent c3>`: exit 0, remote class LOCAL-BEHIND. Same result with `.git/info/grafts` line '<c2> <c3>' (git 2.53.0, no warning). Under --strict the row becomes `behind` (12), so the diverged work is still misreported. The verifier's own scrub (line 78, `git rev-parse --local-env-vars`) unsets GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS and GIT_GRAFT_FILE, so a caller cannot protect the run either. Same class as the round-6 N6-4 'repository-configured code' surface (repository data that changes the verdict); the header does not list it as switched off or as an honest boundary.
findings.control_needle: Same fixture without the replace ref / graft: exit 12 DIVERGED (the instrument sees divergence); with the candidate fix the replaced/grafted fixtures return 12.
findings.candidate_fix: After the env scrub: `export GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/nonexistent` (scratch-tested: replace -> 12, grafts -> 12), plus RED fixtures for both and a paired mutation; consider also the shallow-file member of the class (a shallow repository fails closed to DIVERGED, not a false pass, so it is a lower-risk member).

findings.title: Repository-local ignore rules (.git/info/exclude, a repository core.excludesFile) hide untracked local work
findings.detail: Reproduced: `echo '*' >> .git/info/exclude` plus a new untracked file -> exit 0, dirty false, dirty_untracked 0. The verifier explicitly overrides status.showUntrackedFiles=no because it hides untracked work, but the equivalent uncommitted hiders (info/exclude, repository or global core.excludesFile) are neither overridden nor stated as an honest boundary. Committed .gitignore semantics are legitimate; only the local, unpushed rules are the gap. Owner decision: override core.excludesFile and report ignored files matched only by local rules, or document the boundary.

findings.title: #!/bin/bash -p is bypassed for the worker dispatch: the xargs `bash -c` intermediary sources a caller BASH_ENV
findings.detail: Reproduced: BASH_ENV=<file that appends a line> verify_repos.sh ... -> exit 0 and the caller file ran once (one repository). Line 423 runs `bash -c` without -p. The CPA allowlist (env -i) keeps BASH_ENV out of CPA runs, so impact is limited to standalone runs, but the 2026-10-08 hardening claim 'ignored by the entry process, the run and every helper' does not hold for this helper standalone. Fix: `bash -p -c`, plus a test.
